topics.topic: Enforcement and authoritative recording of completed post-restore reconciliation
questions: What prevents service mode from being enabled before the owner has reapplied every erased, restricted or ended state, and what exact external record is authoritative enough to determine that reconciliation is complete?
What prevents service tokens from being enabled before every required post-backup erasure, restriction and relationship state has been reapplied?
What enforces or records completion of the owner-only recovery reconciliation?

quotes:
The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — before configuring the tokens
   and starting it again.

Registry, which no longer holds those changes,
   cannot list them or tell when this is done.

or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 10).
judgement.divergence: One implementation requires an authoritative completion marker or external attestation before accepting service tokens; another trusts the owner to change configuration at the right time and can start service mode with unreconciled records, which services, affected customers and the owner notice through stale personal-data states.
judgement.why: The required precondition is stated, but neither its authoritative evidence nor any enforceable transition from owner-only to service mode is defined.

topics.topic: Import-file digest algorithm and byte representation
questions: Which digest algorithm and encoding identify the file, and is the digest computed over the exact uploaded bytes or a parsed/canonical representation?
Which digest algorithm is used, and is it computed over the exact uploaded bytes or over a canonicalised parsed representation?
What digest algorithm and byte representation identify an import file?

judgement.why: This is the same import-file digest algorithm and canonical-byte-representation question already assigned to the State 6 format and contract.

precedent.topic: Canonical representation and digest of an import file
quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest.
What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States 5 and 6.
precedent.why: The digest algorithm, canonical byte representation and encoded digest form are format and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie scope, attributes, and deployment constraints
questions: Which cookie attributes and deployment constraint make “only to Registry's own origin” exact, given that cookies are scoped by host and path rather than by origin or port?
What exact cookie domain, path, SameSite and Secure rules implement “only to Registry's own origin,” given that browser cookies are not scoped by port and local access may use HTTP?
What exact cookie scope and attributes implement “own origin,” including deployments where Registry is reached over local HTTP and remote HTTPS?

judgement.why: This is the same owner-session cookie scope, transport and cross-site-policy question already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Exact owner-session cookie scope, transport, and cross-site policy
quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Preserving or reconstructing migration closure across restore
questions: If the first successful import occurred after the restored backup, how does Registry continue to refuse every later import when the migration closure has been lost, despite M10 saying it is present forever?
If the restored backup predates the successful one-time import, is the missing migration closure reconstructed so the operation remains closed, or may Registry accept another import?
How is the fact of a previously successful migration restored or reconstructed when the selected backup predates it?

quotes: None; absent, then present forever.

Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it: numbering continues from the backup's
   last number, and the lost entries exist nowhere.

While the closure exists, uploading and confirming an import are refused
   (R0-79).
judgement.why: M10 says the migration closure remains present forever, while A18 says a closure written after the restored backup is lost, thereby removing the condition that refuses another import.

topics.topic: Preserving the global audit sequence high-water mark across restore
questions: If entries written after the backup had sequence numbers that are lost on restore, may those numbers be issued again, contrary to M09 and A15 saying sequence numbers are never reused and are ordered across every entry ever written?

How can numbering continue from the backup while M09 and A15 require sequence numbers to be one more than the last ever written and never reused, including numbers written after the backup but lost during restore?
After restoring an older backup, how is the global audit high-water mark recovered so a previously issued sequence number is never reused?

quotes:
Sequence numbers are never reused (M09): the next entry after an erasure
   continues from the last number ever written. Registry keeps that last number
   durably, apart from the entries, so neither an erasure nor a restart lowers
   it.

Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it: numbering continues from the backup's
   last number, and the lost entries exist nowhere.
judgement.why: A15 requires numbering to continue above every number ever written, whereas A18 restarts it from the older backup's last number and therefore reuses numbers issued after that backup.

topics.topic: Authenticated backup encryption format and authentication-failure handling
questions: Must backup encryption authenticate the ciphertext and metadata, and what must happen when authentication fails or the wrong key is supplied?
What exact authenticated backup format and cryptographic construction must every backend use?

judgement.why: This is the same authenticated backup encryption format, construction and tamper-detection question already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Required authenticated backup encryption format and tamper detection
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Backup metadata needed for retention and key selection after rotation
questions: How does the owner determine which retained key decrypts a particular backup after several key rotations?
Where are the backup creation time and key identifier kept so automated retention and manual restore still work after key rotation?

quotes:
A backup records its instant, the release that made
   it and the last audit sequence number it holds.

Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its
   making (A17). When the owner changes the key, older backups stay encrypted
   with the key they were made with; the owner keeps that key in the vault
   until the last of them is deleted (R0-23).

Every day at the same run — whether the new backup succeeded or not —
   Registry deletes every backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before.

Restoring production replaces the store with a backup, by the owner on the
   host while Registry is stopped (Explicit exclusions): the owner decrypts it
   with the key it was made with, kept in the vault (rule 3).
judgement.divergence: One implementation keeps readable creation-time and key-selection metadata outside the encrypted payload and can expire and restore rotated-key backups deterministically; another encrypts that metadata or records no key association, so automated retention or the owner's key selection requires trial decryption or can fail, which the owner and backup operation notice.
judgement.why: The rules require age-based deletion and restoration with the original key but do not say how either operation identifies a backup's age and applicable retained key after rotation.

topics.topic: Effect of a rejected replacement upload on the previously accepted file and confirmations
questions: Does an attempted upload that is oversized, unreadable or otherwise refused replace and drop the previously accepted uploaded file?
Does an upload refused for size, unreadable format or another upload-time failure replace and drop the session's previously retained file and invalidate confirmations bound to it?

quotes:
The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in
   the store, until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

at most one uploaded import
file, replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import is accepted.

The import file is read as data with a size limit State 6 sets; nothing in
   it is executed or evaluated, and a file over the limit is refused.
judgement.divergence: One implementation drops the retained file and its bound confirmation as soon as any replacement upload is attempted, even if refused; another retains them unless the new file is accepted, so the owner notices whether the previous mapping can still be confirmed.
judgement.why: The texts say that another upload replaces the file but do not define whether a refused upload counts as that replacement.

topics.topic: Fate of other sessions' uploads and confirmations after a successful import
questions: When one owner session successfully imports, are uploaded files retained by other owner sessions dropped immediately, or do they remain until those sessions end?
When one session successfully imports and creates the migration closure, what happens immediately to uploaded import files and pending import confirmations in every other session?

quotes:
Substitution: two sign-ins are two sessions, each ending on its own; a CSRF
protection is bound to one (R0-29).

at most one uploaded import
file, replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import is accepted.

The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in
   the store, until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

While the closure exists, uploading and confirming an import are refused
   (R0-79).
judgement.divergence: One implementation purges every session's uploaded file and import confirmation when any session commits the import; another drops only the committing session's file and retains sensitive uploads in other sessions until replacement or expiry, which the owner and data-retention controls notice.
judgement.why: Multiple owner sessions may coexist, but the unqualified phrase "the import is accepted" does not define whether cleanup is session-local or global.

topics.topic: Multiplicity and invalidation behavior of concurrent owner sessions
questions: Does a successful sign-in leave earlier owner sessions valid, or invalidate some or all of them?
How many owner sessions may be live, and what does a new sign-in or sign-out do to the others?

judgement.why: This is the same question about concurrent owner sessions and whether a sign-in or sign-out affects other sessions, already answered by P3.

precedent.topic: Multiplicity and replacement or termination semantics of owner sessions
quotes:
Substitution: two sign-ins are two sessions, each ending on its own; a CSRF
protection is bound to one (R0-29).

The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without
   an owner request; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart (M11 is never
   durable).
precedent.why: Two sign-ins create distinct concurrently possible sessions, and each session—including the one presented for sign-out—ends on its own.

topics.topic: Reapplying audit-log erasure cutoffs after restore
questions: How are audit entries erased after the backup's instant removed again after restore, since the reconciliation rule mentions only Customers and projects?
Must disaster-recovery reconciliation reapply the governance cutoff to the restored audit log before normal service resumes?

quotes:
Entries are added by A14 and removed only by
   'erase audit entries before a date' (R0-66); Registry has no other path that
   removes one.

Every change after the backup's instant is
   lost, the audit entries with it: numbering continues from the backup's
   last number, and the lost entries exist nowhere.

The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — before configuring the tokens
   and starting it again.
judgement.divergence: One implementation reapplies the governance cutoff and removes audit entries that had already been erased after the backup; another reconciles only Customers and projects and retains the revived entries until a later review, which the owner and governance retention review notice.
judgement.why: The restore reconciliation explicitly covers Customers and projects but leaves the required treatment of audit entries revived from the backup unspecified.

topics.topic: Reopening and rerunning the injection security review after A19 changed
questions: A19 is named by injection_interpreted_input and browser_boundary and has changed; has A21 been rerun against the revised rule, or is its “PERFORMED” result currently reopened?
Has the injection review been repeated against the changed A19 rule, and what is the resulting accepted evidence?

quotes: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
Every decision a category names is accepted.
Security review: PERFORMED
- injection_interpreted_input: APPLICABLE; references: A02, A16, A19; affected: M03, M08, import file, every stored text value
- browser_boundary: APPLICABLE; references: A13, A19; affected: owner interface, CSRF protection, session cookie, rendering of agent-written text
judgement.why: The current performed and accepted A21 review expressly includes A19 in both affected categories, and the text supplies no later A19 change that would reopen it.

topics.topic: Schema representation and validity of historical pointers with removed artifact types
questions: How can a retained pointer still satisfy M05's rule that its type is one of the vocabulary the specification declares, and how do output schemas represent a removed type that is now “unknown”?
How can current-release schemas represent a historical pointer whose type is no longer declared?

quotes:
its type, one of the vocabulary the specification declares, and so its owner
  service, which the vocabulary fixes (R0-33; "Declared vocabularies");

A release that removes a type keeps every pointer of it, with its status as
   it was: 'list artifacts' still carries all of them, and the agent
   projection, which carries only `published` pointers (State 1, "Projections
   and answers"), still carries its published one.

After the removal, publishing that type and 'read the latest artifact of a
   type' for it are refused as an unknown type, and withdrawing a pointer of it
   is refused.
judgement.why: M05 requires every pointer's type to belong to the specification's declared vocabulary, while A22 requires pointers whose now-unknown type has been removed from that vocabulary to remain and be returned.

topics.topic: Temporal invariants across imported projects and their related records
questions: Must an archived imported project's last-changed instant equal its archived instant, as required by the Project revision/time rules, or may the two differ so long as neither precedes creation?
Which cross-record time relationships must an imported project, its rooms and its pointers satisfy?

quotes:
Archiving moves it once and
  records the archived date.

A record the import brings in keeps the instants its source holds: a
  project's created, last-changed and archived instants, a room's added
  instant, a pointer's published and superseded instants.

a record was changed,
   archived or superseded before it was created, added or published.
missing name refused; unknown or archived project refused; a second room of the same name is a second room (R0-10); a project the session is not granted refused

Publishing and withdrawing on an archived project are refused (R0-17);
   reading stays open.
judgement.divergence: One implementation refuses an import unless an archived project's last-changed instant equals its archived instant and every room addition and pointer publication precedes archiving; another checks only the temporal comparisons expressly listed in A16 and accepts later related records or differing instants, which the owner notices through import acceptance and the resulting history.
judgement.why: The normal lifecycle implies additional temporal relationships, but A16's exact malformed-record conditions neither require them nor state whether imported history is exempt.

topics.topic: Abuse controls for repeated invalid service-token attempts
questions: What abuse control, if any, applies to repeated wrong service-token attempts, and who owns detecting or throttling them? A13 defines only owner sign-in lockout, while A09 and A17 define rights and startup validation.

topics.topic: Atomic publication, detection, and cleanup of interrupted backup files
questions: How are process crashes or host failures during backup publication distinguished from valid backups and cleaned up on the next start or run?

topics.topic: Backend obligation and evidence for structural separation of queries and commands
questions: What backend obligation and verification demonstrate that caller values cannot alter query or command structure?

topics.topic: Configuration namespace, syntax, and malformed-item rules
questions: What is the configuration's concrete namespace and syntax, and what makes each non-secret item malformed rather than merely unusable, especially when configuration is supplied through an environment containing unrelated variables?

topics.topic: Coverage of derived data and interpreter boundaries by interpreted-input protection
questions: Does the prohibition cover transformed or derived caller data and every interpreter boundary, including templates, paths, regular expressions and configuration fragments?

topics.topic: Data classification of personal values in pending import confirmations
questions: What class applies to personal values retained as part of a pending import confirmation?

topics.topic: How Cabinet Kernel operations determine the target project
questions: For each Cabinet Kernel operation, is `project_id` required, optional with active-project fallback, or derived from another record such as the pointer?

topics.topic: Malformed imported object kinds, characteristics, and pointer values
questions: Are an object kind outside its declared vocabulary, undeclared object characteristics, and a pointer with neither a nonblank uri nor a nonblank payload_ref malformed, and how are they reported?

topics.topic: Ordering artifact operations against concurrent project lifecycle changes
questions: What orders a publish or withdrawal against a concurrent archive, anonymisation or whole deletion of the same project, especially for an owner call not covered by A10's agent-call ordering?

topics.topic: Permitted path relationships among stores, backups, and verification files
questions: Which path relationships between the store, backup directory and temporary verification files are permitted?

topics.topic: Presentation and confirmation of imported object mapping
questions: Where are the imported object's address, kind and characteristics shown and confirmed, even though the import carries the object and the owner must check the mapping before applying it?

topics.topic: Project selection when an import contains duplicate project IDs
questions: How can the owner pick one project when the file contains two project records with the same project id, and does picking that id bring both duplicate records into validation?

topics.topic: Refusal precedence when multiple checks fail within one A04 stage
questions: What exact refusal wins when two or more checks in the same stage fail?

topics.topic: Replay safety for request IDs lost by restoring an older backup
questions: What happens when a caller retries a create or publish whose committed record and request id were lost by restore: must A01 still prevent a duplicate, or is replay safety explicitly limited to history retained in the restored store?

topics.topic: Response to request-ID collisions outside the caller's authorized projects
questions: What answer is returned when Kernel supplies a request id already attached to a room or pointer in a project outside its granted set?

topics.topic: Retention of request IDs after anonymisation, deletion, or erasure
questions: After a Project is anonymised or deleted, or a Customer is erased, must its former request id remain reserved so an old retry cannot create a duplicate?

topics.topic: Same-day retry policy after a failed backup run
questions: If today's run fails and Registry restarts later that same UTC day, must it retry because no backup was made, or must it wait because a run already occurred?

topics.topic: Secret representation used for length, equality, and authentication
questions: Are secrets raw bytes, encoded text decoded to bytes, or Unicode text, and on which representation are length, equality and authentication comparisons performed?

topics.topic: Validation treatment of malformed records in unselected projects
questions: Are malformed records belonging only to unpicked projects reported or ignored?

topics.topic: Whether ended agent-session identities may be reused
questions: Must Registry prevent reuse of an ended session identity, or may one identity denote multiple sessions and make old audit references ambiguous?

topics.topic: Which model or classification changes reopen security reviews
questions: Do changes to an affected model or data classification also reopen the relevant browser, files, authorization and concurrency reviews?
